upsertPapers.title: On the expected performance of a parallel algorithm for finding maximal independent subsets of a random graph
Local algorithms for independent sets are half-optimal

upsertSlices.label: Random-input independent sets: algorithm and locality
upsertSlices.task: Supplied random graphs, prescribed greedy behavior, and maximum-size local algorithms have distinct contracts.
assumptions: The upper panel measures expected iterations of PARALLEL-GREEDY. The lower panel measures solution density within fixed-radius local algorithms. Neither red statement is a universal MIS computational lower bound.

axis.label: See scoped figure panels; incompatible objectives have separate axes

results.notes: Red bounds constrain PARALLEL-GREEDY only. Each iteration costs O(1) CRCW PRAM time with a processor per edge; no universal MIS time lower bound is claimed.

results.notes: Radius may depend on λ and accuracy but not n. The red bound is only for factor-of-i.i.d./fixed-radius local algorithms. Unrestricted optimum is asymptotically twice this density; that is structural context, not a runtime lower bound.
